beats.narration_en: Your seatbelt is built to give way on purpose.
In a crash it first snaps tight,
pulling you back into the seat.
Then a twisting metal bar in the reel starts to give,
Your chest gets a longer, gentler stop.
A belt with no give stops it almost at once, with a harder push.
Same idea as a crumple zone: a longer stop means a smaller peak force.
